claim: Pausing and restarting gives a small real gain on creative and insight problems for people (d about 0.3), larger for divergent tasks, smaller when the break task is demanding.
agent_test: Same budget: one long attempt vs attempt, fresh-context restart with a different framing, attempt; compare solve rate.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A break helps only if the filler does not load the same resource; an idle gap does nothing for an LLM, which has no hidden process between calls.
agent_test: Insert (a) nothing, (b) unrelated light task, (c) heavy task between attempts; compare at equal tokens. Expect only restart-with-new-context to matter.

claim: Unconscious thought (distraction before choosing) has no reliable advantage over deliberation; the small meta effect vanishes after bias correction and a 399-person replication found null.
schema_part: G (do not trust a hidden stage)
agent_test: Not needed; use as a design guard. Check by comparing deliberate vs unverified one-shot choice.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Verbalising does not reliably hurt insight problems: the candle problem showed 23.5% vs 27.7% box solutions, while the original Schooler coin result (45.8% vs 35.6%) is a single-lab effect.
schema_part: G (written rationale allowed on text reasoning)
agent_test: No-rationale vs rationale arm on insight-style items at equal tokens.

claim: Impasse is not needed for insight; those who hit an impasse in the candle problem solved less often (1/15 vs 7/19). Restructuring also occurs in non-insight solutions.
schema_part: O (reframe operator available at any state, not only after a stall)
agent_test: Trigger reframe at fixed step counts vs only after detected stall; compare.

claim: Insight solutions in humans correlate with verbal working memory in one study but survive working-memory load in another, so the pure ordinary-process view is not fully supported.
schema_part: S (two routes: stepwise search and cheap associative route)
agent_test: Test whether cheap wide sampling plus check beats stepwise-only at equal tokens on insight items.

claim: Most correct insight answers are already correct as fast first responses, and few are corrected later. (LLM analog: in o1-like math runs the first solution round already holds the correct answer in >92% of cases, but no insight-item test.)
agent_test: Compare final answer vs first sample on remote-associate items; count non-corrections.

claim: Chain of thought can lower LLM accuracy on tasks where verbal thinking hurts people (artificial grammar: GPT-4o 87.5 to 64.4; exception learning up to 331% more passes), but not for all models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet +1.8, n.s.).
agent_test: Pilot each task class with and without rationale; choose by measured result.

claim: Written reasoning is not the whole computation: blocking CoT barely changes strong models on CRT.
agent_test: Compare answers with rationale hidden vs shown on trap items.

claim: Plain LLM sampling gives little true variety: within-prompt similarity 0.82 across 42 models, 61.2% of pairs above 0.8 even under min-p; LLM populations are less variable than humans.
agent_test: Measure pairwise distinctness of N samples under plain vs operator-forced prompts at equal tokens.

claim: Temperature is a weak creativity lever: novelty coefficient 0.308 with incoherence cost; helps mid models unstably, not GPT-4.
schema_part: O (do not use temperature as the variation operator)
agent_test: Compare temperature sweep vs structured variation at equal tokens.

claim: Remote cross-domain cues raise human originality but give LLMs no average benefit; only the top two models gained, for distant sources.
schema_part: O (test each variation operator on the agent)
agent_test: Add distant-source cue arm vs none; score originality and correctness.

claim: Divergent-then-convergent prompting helped GPT-4 efficiency (+6.5%) and self-reflection cut infeasible solutions (-9.7%) on MacGyver; gains are a few points and model dependent.
agent_test: Replicate generate-wide-then-check vs single answer at equal tokens.

claim: Overgenerating and filtering ideas beats single-pass generation in novelty (5.64 AI vs 4.84 human; 5.81 with human rerank), but diversity plateaus (about 5% non-duplicate of 4000) and LLM self-ranking is unreliable.
agent_test: Sweep N samples with dedup; check where diversity saturates.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace 'aha' shifts in small RL-tuned models are rare and lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44%); a code-triggered reconsideration at high entropy gave +8.41 points on MATH-500 for small models, but only +0.45 on crosswords and about 0 on Rush Hour.
agent_test: Trigger re-ask by entropy/disagreement rule vs random vs never at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs recognise the right answer poorly on insight riddles: reasoning models 17.6% vs non-reasoning 7.6% vs humans 52.9%; right candidates often appear in thought logs but are not endorsed.
agent_test: Compare model self-acceptance vs external verifier on riddle items.

claim: LLM creative output matches or exceeds humans on output measures (AUT, DAT, RAT) but process measures differ: model associations stay nearer the cue and representational change is weak.
agent_test: Process-trace metrics (distance travelled, reframe count) alongside output score.

claim: Reasoning-style tuning can move model representations away from default-mode-like creative patterns.
agent_test: Compare reasoning vs non-reasoning models on divergent tasks at equal tokens.

claim: No direct LLM test of the EII theory or of incubation has been published in the sources found; the EII loop has only been fit to old human data.
agent_test: Run plain loop vs loop with separate wide-sampling and check stages.

claim: EII's own human data fits are to prior data: priming t(2100)=8.5, reminiscence rising 2.90 to 5.00 over 0 to 10 min, with simulation matches; no new predictions except the distractor study (N=114).
agent_test: Reference only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Honing theory evidence is from one lab (small judged samples, e.g. 29 honing vs 13 structure-mapping, chi2=4.57) and has not been independently replicated or tested on LLMs.
agent_test: Keep blended draft vs discrete candidates under multiple framings at equal tokens.

claim: Verbal overshadowing is real for faces in a registered replication but is narrow; it is not a general law.
agent_test: See K08.

claim: Of the cheap variation operators tested on current LLMs, persona modifiers plus a short plan (CoT) before each idea, in-context regeneration, and verbalized sampling raise distinctness; temperature, paraphrase and 'be creative' system prompts give little. Not compared at equal tokens in one study.
agent_tests: operator-by-operator comparison with a meaning-based dedup count at equal tokens

claim: Wide independent sampling plus a reliable check scales with sample count; without a reliable verifier, voting and reward models plateau after a few hundred samples. At equal compute, sequential revision wins on easy items and parallel sampling on hard ones.
agent_tests: equal-token arms on insight-type items with and without a rule check

claim: CoT gains are concentrated in math, symbolic and logic tasks (mean +14.2, +12.3, +6.9 points); other categories show about +0.7. Longer reasoning can hurt on distractor and spurious-pattern tasks. A task-class rule for rationale is supported but not tested on insight items with current models.
agent_tests: rationale on vs off per task class on current models

claim: Wrong early commitments persist in context: multi-turn LLM performance drops 39% on average and a recap recovers only 15-20% of it. This suggests a fresh-context restart should drop the failed attempt, but no direct LLM incubation or restart test exists.
agent_tests: fresh-context restart with question and surviving constraints only vs continued loop at equal tokens

claim: Verbal overshadowing on insight is mixed: Schooler 1993 (secondhand: 25% vs 5% drop, interaction 20%), a tighter replication found no clear interaction (57 vs 53% insight, 48 vs 48% non-insight, BF 0.92 insensitive), a small T-puzzle study leans toward a cost (OR 5.0).
